newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends barely higher, still ranging.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends barely higher, still ranging.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly higher in quiet steady trade although the market still appeared unsure of which direction to follow as rallies continued to fizzle despite low LME stocks, traders said.
Brent Tolen of Triland USA Inc said copper was locked in a tug of war between key short and long partcipants within an 86 to 93 cents per pound range.
The market was waiting for each side to make its move.
"People are no longer falling off their chairs anymore if stocks are down. It's not a big deal. We all know about the stocks, it's what the price thinks of it," Tolen said.
On price direction, Tolen added he was "still leaning on the upside."
The LME November options declaration passed uneventfully Wednesday in London, barely causing a ripple before or after the event.
A broker said no major changes were expected from Friday's LME stock report.
December COMEX settled 0.60 cent firmer at 92.65 cents a lb, traded 93.20 to 92.40 cents. Spot November went out 0.40 cent higher at 93.50 cents.
